skill.name: algorithmic-art
skill.description: Create original generative art with p5.js, seeded randomness, interactive controls, and reusable HTML viewer templates.
skill.summary: Build interactive p5.js generative art from an algorithmic philosophy and reproducible seed controls.
skill.author: anthropics

security_audit.summary: Manual review confirmed only low-severity external network dependencies for p5.js and Google Fonts in the HTML template. The command execution, script execution, and reconnaissance alerts are false positives from Markdown code fences, inline code, prose, and JavaScript RegExp use. No prompt injection or hidden malicious behavior was found.

remediation.issue: Generated viewers load p5.js and fonts from external CDNs.
remediation.suggestion: Document the external requests clearly or provide a bundled offline template for environments that restrict network access.

content.value_statement: Creating original generative art often requires both aesthetic direction and working interactive code. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to produce p5.js artwork with seeded variation and user controls.
actual_capabilities: Creates an algorithmic philosophy before implementation.
Builds single-file HTML viewers based on the included p5.js template.
Adds seed controls for previous, next, random, and specific seed exploration.
Defines interactive sliders and color controls for artwork parameters.
Supports reproducible outputs through p5.js randomSeed and noiseSeed.
Provides a JavaScript reference template for generative art structure.
limitations: Generated viewers depend on p5.js and fonts loaded from external CDNs by default.
The skill creates code and concepts, not rendered image files by itself.
Very complex animations may need performance tuning after generation.
It should create original styles rather than copy living artists or copyrighted works.

use_cases.description: Create an interactive artwork with controllable parameters and repeatable seed variations.

use_cases.title: Teach creative coding concepts
use_cases.description: Show how seeded randomness, particles, noise fields, and controls combine into generative systems.

use_cases.title: Explore visual directions quickly
use_cases.description: Generate browser-ready art prototypes that support rapid exploration of palettes, motion, and composition.

prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when specific parameters matter.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create generative art about magnetic fields. Add controls for particle count, field strength, trail length, and palette colors.

prompt_templates.title: Design a seeded variation set
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when you want repeatable outputs.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a reproducible p5.js artwork with seed navigation. Highlight five seed values that produce distinct compositions.

prompt_templates.title: Build a refined art direction
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this for advanced creative coding work.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a gallery-quality algorithmic artwork using recursive growth, controlled chaos, and subtle motion. Keep the reference concept abstract and original.

output_examples.input: Create generative art inspired by wind moving through tall grass.
output_examples.output: The result includes a short computational philosophy and an interactive browser artwork with seeded flow, motion controls, and palette controls.

output_examples.input: Make an abstract particle system with reproducible variations.
output: A single HTML artifact opens in a browser without setup.
Sliders adjust particle density, motion speed, and trail behavior.

best_practices: Start with a clear theme, mood, or system behavior rather than a named artist style.
Ask for the seed values and parameters you want users to explore.
Test the generated HTML in a browser and tune performance for the target device.
anti_patterns: Do not ask it to copy a specific artist or copyrighted visual work.
Do not remove seed controls if reproducible variation matters.
Do not request many heavy particle systems without performance limits.

faq.question: Does this skill create finished images?
faq.answer: It creates interactive p5.js HTML artwork. You can export images from the browser if the generated viewer includes export controls.

faq.question: Can outputs be reproduced?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill requires seeded randomness, so the same seed and parameters should produce the same artwork.

faq.question: Does the viewer work offline?
faq.answer: Not by default. The template loads p5.js and fonts from external CDNs unless you modify it to bundle those assets.

faq.question: Can I control colors and motion?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill guides the model to add sliders, color pickers, and other controls that match the artwork.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report marks it as compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is this safe for commercial design work?
faq.answer: Use it to create original visual systems. Avoid prompts that copy specific artists, brands, or copyrighted works.
